title: Ideal powers vanish under cohomology reduction
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a morphism, and $J=I\mathcal O_X$ its extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Let $F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $p,n\in\mathbb N$. Write $C(G)=H^p(X,G)$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], restricted to $A$ through $A\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For the canonical quotient projection $\pi_n:F\to F/J^nF$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], one has $I^n C(F)\subseteq\ker C(\pi_n)$. There are no properness, coherence or Noetherian hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 02OC, theorem-formal-functions: construction of maps H^p(F)/I^n H^p(F) -> H^p(F/I^n F); parent proof step 1

proof.text: For $a\in I^n$, its image in global functions belongs to $J^n$, since $J$ is generated by images of $I$. Multiplication by this function factors through the image $J^nF\hookrightarrow F$ and its composite with the cokernel projection is zero. At $n=0$ the quotient is zero.

Apply module cohomology to the multiplication endomorphism. Its induced map is multiplication by the same global function. Functoriality and additivity take the zero composite to zero, so $C(\pi_n)(a x)=0$ for every class $x$.
Linearity of $C(\pi_n)$ and closure of its kernel under addition show that it contains the submodule generated by all $a x$, namely $I^n C(F)$.
